rationale: Mississippi State is 4-4 and must win all four remaining regular-season games (Vanderbilt, Auburn, Tennessee Tech, at Ole Miss) to reach 8 wins. Model game probabilities multiply to roughly 4.5-6%, with the Egg Bowl at No. 10 Ole Miss (~14%) as the binding constraint. The starting QB is out for the season and backup AJ Swann's arm injury may force a struggling freshman to start, which models likely underweight, and the team is on a four-game losing streak with a sputtering offense. Positive correlation between wins (a healthy QB lifts every game) slightly offsets this. Net, I estimate about 4%.

Greenland has never scheduled an independence referendum despite broad nominal support, because of economic dependence on Denmark. The current majority coalition (Demokraatit/IA/Atassut, ~19/31 seats) favours a gradual path, is waiting for the §21 commission due in late 2026, and on Nov 3 rejected even a referendum on the defence deal. No independence-referendum motion has been found on the autumn agenda, and Inatsisartut's multi-reading procedure makes passing a new resolution within 9 days nearly impossible. The remaining probability covers a loose ruling by the contest judges, a sudden crisis-driven reversal, or a pending item the research missed.

Preliminary 2026 counts are about 122.7–124.3M ballots, while exceeding 46.8% of a plausible 247–252M CVAP needs only about 116–118M, a cushion of roughly 5–8M ballots or 2–3 points. California and Washington are still counting, so totals will only rise. Independent signals agree: McDonald's VEP rate of about 49.4% vs 46.1% in 2022, state turnout records, and record early voting. The paths to NO would require an implausibly large CVAP (about 265M) or an unexplained 6M+ shortfall in the EAVS ballots-counted total. The remaining risk is mostly reliance on second-hand figures, EAVS reporting quirks, and resolution procedure, which affects timing more than direction.

Carbon's announcement mirrors Argon's exactly, and Argon's 13-day lag points to Tue Nov 10, inside the window; the introductory-pricing link to Argon's Nov 30 end date and the AI Studio identifiers hint at a November launch. However, Google frames Carbon as a bigger cyber-capability jump with US government testing, and Google appeared to still be iterating on checkpoints after the announcement (new Arena checkpoint ~Oct 31), which argues for longer gating. As of Nov 6 there are no public-facing signs of an imminent launch: no Fairwind update, no app strings, no 'big week' hints. Even if release by end of November is somewhat likely (~55-60%), much of that mass could fall Nov 16-25, so hitting this exact week is roughly a coin flip conditional on a November release.

Nunes is a 38-year-old returning after ~41 months to face a prime, never-finished Olympic judoka champion whose grappling-pressure style mirrors the only loss of Nunes's peak (Peña). Over five rounds, rust and Nunes's known late-fight cardio issues favor Harrison. Offsetting this, Harrison is coming off neck surgery with a reportedly late and short camp and has had difficult weight cuts, and Nunes has a real early-KO path against Harrison's less refined striking entries. Cancellation resolves at fair price, so I forecast conditional on the fight happening; draws add a negligible half-credit. Net, I put Nunes slightly below the anchor at ~36%.

The 10-year sits around 4.84-4.85 on the Treasury par basis and needs a print of 4.75 or lower within about 15 business days. Volatility is elevated after a 40+ bp October decline and a tech-led equity rout. A driftless first-passage model with daily closes gives about 60-65%. I shade down because the latest leg was a safe-haven bid prone to reversal, the early-September floor of 4.77-4.80 may hold, ADP beat and CPI has been hot, and the Treasury print runs slightly above vendor closes. Offsetting this, the 2-year's 11 bp drop shows real repricing of Fed hike odds, the downtrend is strong, and today's payrolls, Nov 10 CPI and Nvidia earnings could all trigger a 10 bp move.

YES requires a price-range S-1/A and roadshow launch by roughly Nov 10-12, yet as of Nov 5 no range was filed. Meanwhile a $2.5T AI-driven Nasdaq drawdown hit and anchor investors are pushing the valuation down from ~$1.5T toward ~$1T. WSJ and Reuters both report that delay is being actively considered and that investors doubt a roadshow next week. Even on the original plan the deadline had only about 2 trading days of slack, and some reports put the target at simply 'before Thanksgiving', so even a short slip resolves NO. Anthropic's strong incentive to proceed at a cut valuation, and the near-certainty of pricing once a mega-deal launches, keep this from being a longshot below 10%.

The outgoing GOP House could hold a party-line rule vote that resolves YES even if the bill is pulled, as happened with the SCORE Act in Dec 2025. Trump's backing and the 'last chance' framing add pressure. However, the Democratic midterm win removes Democratic incentive to help, the GOP is split on employee-status language, the margin is razor-thin with possible absences, and the CR/NDAA deadlines crowd a short calendar. Leadership's usual pattern is to whip the bill and pull it before any recorded vote, and nothing is on the floor schedule yet. A must-pass vehicle would likely not count.

The blockade is in force and Trump has consistently tied lifting it to a signed deal, which held in June. An active Qatari draft makes lifting the blockade the US's Day-1 step, and Vance plus post-midterm politics push toward a deal, so this window is above the base rate. But Iran says the sides are far apart and calls the US offer unconvincing, hawks in the administration favour keeping the leverage, and CENTCOM is preparing to resume strikes. Only about 9 days remain, and a deal announced in conditional or future-dated terms would not qualify. Net, roughly double the base rate.

The story is very likely the Ecuadorian priest killed by a falling crucifix on Oct 17. Its best chances to air were Oct 25 and Nov 1, and neither appears to have mentioned it. Only two episodes remain in the window (Nov 8, Nov 15). Those will likely cover the midterm aftermath and the season finale, and the story will be 3-4 weeks old by then. Mocking a non-villainous person's accidental death is off-brand for Oliver, and Catholic outlets were already pushing back on such jokes. A small residual covers a throwaway or montage joke, a web-exclusive counting toward resolution, or a misidentified screenshot.

With 24 days left, the status quo has Anthropic's Opus 5.5 at ~1810 and Google's best entry, Gemini 4 Carbon, at #4 and ~42 points behind, a gap that score drift alone almost never closes. A YES needs Google to add a new checkpoint or a higher-effort Carbon variant scoring above ~1810 before Nov 30. A new checkpoint is being tested on Arena and a developer release is rumoured within weeks, so a new entry has perhaps a 40-50% chance. Even so, Google's recent WebDev debuts landed at #4-8, so a new entry would probably reach #1 only about 30% of the time. Possible competitor releases add a modest further discount.

Under the likely per-minute 60-second trimmed-mean reading, YES only needs BTC to hold below $72.5K for about a minute, a 4.2% further drop with 24 days left. Barrier math puts that at about 65-70%, trimmed to about 60% because brief wicks are filtered out, $75-76K support held in Sep/Oct, and liquidation flushes often mean-revert. Risk-off momentum (the Nasdaq correction, ETF outflows, the Binance hack aftermath, Nvidia earnings ahead) keeps the downside path very live. There is a real chance (~20%) that the literal cumulative running-trimmed-mean reading applies, in which case YES needs a sustained regime near $68-70K and is only about 10-15% likely. Blending the two readings gives a little over 50%.

CPHC advisories put Lala at 125 mph on Aug 18, 2026, and still at about 115 mph (Category 3) on Aug 19, well above the 111 mph threshold, and multiple independent outlets reported it as a major hurricane. Secondary sources list an even higher peak of about 130 mph, so any best-track revision looks upward rather than downward. The storm dissipated in late August, and no other 'Lala' can occur before the deadline. The only routes to NO are an extreme best-track downgrade below 96 kt or an administrative misresolution or void. The fact that the market is still listed open is most likely a settlement delay (for example, waiting on the final Tropical Cyclone Report) or a stale listing, and I discount it only slightly.

The Dow closed at 51,523 after a 3.4% AI-driven rout, with futures pointing toward ~51,000, leaving roughly a 6-7% further decline needed within ~16 sessions. At current VIX-implied volatility a barrier model gives ~19-24%, but Dow-specific vol is lower and implied vol after spikes tends to overstate realized vol. The Dow is less tech-heavy and was cushioned relative to the Nasdaq. Upcoming catalysts (CPI with a hawkish Fed, Nvidia earnings Nov 17) give real tail risk, and fat tails and contagion keep this well above a calm-market base rate. Thanksgiving seasonality, the usual dip-buying after one-off shocks, and a possibly shortened window via the Nov 25 close date pull it down.

The market appears conditional: if no clear left/right polarization is judged, it most likely resolves N/A, so the relevant probability is the direction given that it resolves. On both elite policy (Trump/Sacks acceleration, preemption, pro-data-center rhetoric versus post-midterm Democratic calls for moratoriums, pauses and investigations of 'AI billionaires') and mass attitudes (Republicans consistently more favourable in polls), the right is the pro-AI side. AI's opposition coalition of environmental, labor and progressive groups also matches the reference-class pattern where the right ends up pro. The main NO risk is a resolver without a parent market reading the GOP populist anti-data-center turn (Hawley, DeSantis, Abbott) as making the right not clearly pro-AI, or subjective idiosyncrasy. A genuine reversal with the left as the pro-AI side before Nov 30 looks very unlikely.

Iran and Oman have talked for 7 months and issued only a 'proposed framework' (Aug 25) that evidently did not qualify; the latest Nov 5 readout is explicit ongoing-consultation language. Oman publicly ties any implementation to a U.S.–Iran settlement and faces explicit U.S. threats and sanctions warnings over an Iran–Oman control or toll role, so a standalone agreement is unlikely. The main YES path needs a U.S.–Iran deal within ~3 weeks amid active escalation (strikes, mines), and then a formal Iran–Oman announcement soon after, whereas the June template deferred Iran–Oman administration by 60 days. Reports that the bilateral text is essentially 'concluded' add some tail upside if a U.S.–Iran deal lands quickly. The strict 'declarative acceptance' rule also screens out the recurring unilateral Iranian claims and framework-style statements.

Outcome depends almost entirely on the creator's resolution behavior, since no public evidence will exist about a private person's sex life. The creator overwhelmingly cancels joke Gwern markets, often years late, and this topic is more sensitive than most, which raises N/A odds. The YES resolution of the related relationship-by-2030 market is the main reason to sit above the raw 7% base rate, because the creator might treat it as implying YES here. Late or absent resolution and possible moderation further favour not-YES. Net: roughly 13%.

Rockstar has declined a steady ~13% YoY for three straight quarters, driven by planned 2026 SKU cuts that won't lap until 2027. The one available Carbon Arc reading (87.4) matches Circana, so YES needs a ~10-point jump. Management's 'green shoots' and stable-QoQ comments point to stabilization, not a sharp YoY recovery, and the turnaround plans are framed for 2027. The remaining YES probability comes from receipt-panel noise for a small brand, possible panel or brand-mapping changes, and an unknown November 2025 base. The missing September and October Carbon Arc readings are the main source of uncertainty.

Bangladesh's a cappella entry 'Tumi Ele' was ranked last of 11 by Aussievision's pundit team and is not among the leaders of any fan poll found. Malaysia, the Philippines, South Korea, host Thailand and other Southeast Asian entries look stronger, and six Southeast Asian countries could vote as a bloc. Bangladesh's large domestic audience cannot vote for its own entry, and its diaspora counts only through the single Rest-of-the-World set, 1 of 12 public-vote sets. Because this is a first-edition contest with a small field and Asian juries whose tastes may differ from Western fan sites, there is extra variance, and a distinctive vocal act could surprise. Even so, an outsider would need to land exactly 3rd, which keeps the probability well below the naive 9%.

Only 23 days remain, and the status quo is no second claim. The strongest YES lead is the Sept 17 single-source report that OpenAI was 'close' on Hodge. It has produced nothing in 7+ weeks, the Oct 6 release had only special cases, and a K3 Hodge paper was withdrawn for a sign error. Reputational damage from the Navier–Stokes credit dispute and the backlash against bulk releases pushes OpenAI toward slower, coordinated announcements. The remaining problems (RH, P vs NP, Yang–Mills) look far harder than Navier–Stokes was. Upside risk comes from Altman's 'we have more results' comment and a possible next-GPT launch in November that could serve as a showcase.

Pierce re-signed in March 2026 on a 4-year, $114M deal with $60M fully guaranteed at signing and a $26M signing bonus, so a trade would speed up dead money. He is on IR with no return timetable, which makes him unattractive to buyers. Fire-sale coverage (SI, Covers) explicitly names him as an exception to the Colts' sell-off, and the live trade talks involve Taylor and Downs. The trade deadline is Nov 10, after which only a release-and-claim, effectively impossible given his guarantees, could move him before Nov 30. The main residual risk is uncertainty about Kalshi's exact settlement mechanics, which I could not verify, plus a small chance of a shock deadline trade by an aggressive new regime.

YES requires a price-range S-1/A and roadshow launch around Nov 9-10 followed by a ~6-7 trading-day roadshow, pricing by Thursday Nov 19 and first trade by Friday Nov 20; there is essentially no slack. As of Nov 7 no price range has been filed, and a credible Reuters exclusive (four sources) reports investor doubts about launching next week and a possible postponement amid the AI sell-off and valuation pushback. Countervailing: WSJ and IFR reported Anthropic pushing ahead for a Nov 16-week debut, and an on-schedule launch next week would make YES roughly a coin flip.

On 28 Feb 2026 Iran's SNSC and government mass texts told Tehran's residents to leave the city. Read literally, that is plausibly an 'attempt at an evacuation' by Iran's government, and it almost certainly falls inside the roughly Dec 2025–Dec 2026 window. Against that, the call was voluntary and conditional, the question was framed around the drought scenario, and the market apparently stayed open for months afterward, which hints the creator may not count it. If February is rejected, a new call needs full-scale strikes on Tehran to resume within about 25 days; that is possible given the post-midterm debate, but probably no more than about 10% overall. A water-driven evacuation is negligible.

Multiple independent outlets report Susurkaev withdrew from UFC 334, Cesar Almeida replaced him against Donte Johnson, and Susurkaev is now booked against Damian Pinas at UFC 335 on Dec 12. Under the rules, a cancelled fight resolves to a Kalshi-determined 'fair price', not YES, and the Johnson-Almeida bout cannot be won by Susurkaev. YES requires reinstating the original pairing within 48 hours of the original start and a Susurkaev win (~65% if it happened), so the joint chance is tiny. I leave a small residual for reporting errors and the unusual fair-price/settlement mechanics. Note that the expected payout differs from P(YES), because the fair-price settlement may be well above zero.

Multiple independent sources report META's Nov 5, 2026 regular-hours low at $583.80, corroborated by timestamped intraday prints of $587.39 at 10:50 AM ET and $594.17, well below the $600 strike. Pyth aggregation differences cannot plausibly erase a ~$16 margin sustained over many minutes, and the exchange daily low is the fallback if Pyth data is missing. The main residual risk is that the market was created after the Nov 5 lows, which is unlikely for a monthly market typically listed before the month starts. Even then, META at ~$610 with very high volatility and ~16 sessions left would touch $600 with roughly 80-88% probability. One conflicting Investing.com row (low 613.44) appears to be a data error.

All seven 2026 decisions so far appear to have matched heavily favored outcomes (>90% near decision), so the question mostly depends on whether the Dec 8 favorite is right. The Fed historically almost never surprises the day-before favorite at scheduled meetings, and pricing typically firms up by then; a December hike is currently ~70–85% favored. I shade below the historical base rate because Chair Warsh opposes forward guidance, the committee is divided, and key data (CPI, PCE, Dec 4 jobs) could leave pricing closer to a coin flip. I also apply a small discount because the creator might score a past meeting (e.g., September) differently, since Polymarket's own prices weren't verified, and because of ambiguity around ties or emergency moves.

BTC sits near $75.8k and needs a sustained one-minute BRTI print above $85k (+12%) within ~23.5 days. Volatility models put a touch at roughly 25-33%, but the regime is bearish: lower highs, ETF outflows, BTC below its 20- and 50-day averages, and Fed hike odds near 80%. 2026's record-low implied vol and October's ±7% range suggest typical moves are smaller than history implies, and the minute-trimmed mean filters wicks. Offsetting this, the Nov 5 liquidation flush, the Nov 10 CPI and AI-earnings catalysts, and the fact that $85k traded only five weeks ago keep a relief-rally path plausible. Net, I shade modestly below the volatility-model midpoint.

The structural prior strongly favours the KMT incumbent: Taipei's blue lean, incumbency, a consolidated opposition with no TPP candidate, and a midterm environment that tends to punish the governing DPP. Shen has closed a large gap since May. TVBS's series fell from Chiang +28 to +4, and blue-leaning UDN even showed Shen +4, so the race is genuinely competitive. However, the most recent neutral or blue-leaning poll (ETtoday, Nov 1-3) still has Chiang +8.8, and the green-leaning polls showing Shen +17 have large house effects that I discount heavily. Most polls also show voters expecting Chiang to win, and in Taipei undecided voters have historically consolidated toward the blue side late. Weighing the polls and the momentum against the fundamentals, Shen is a real but clear underdog at about 30%.

The front has been near-stalemate since February, with BBG monthly figures mostly within ±200 km² of zero. Negative months have come almost only from discrete Ukrainian local counteroffensives (Huliaipole in Feb, Lyman/Komar in Sept). As of Nov 6 there is no sign of a new Ukrainian operation; reports describe Ukraine holding against heavy Russian pressure on Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka, while DeepState shows Russia's tempo slowing to ~50 km² per four weeks. With no operation, BBG's conservative crediting of Ukrainian gains and autumn infiltration conditions favour a small positive figure, though Ukrainian October gains confirmed late could tip it negative. Combining about a 22% chance of a meaningful Ukrainian push (mostly YES) with about 20% YES otherwise gives roughly a third, in line with the 2026 base rate.

Grillo is -7 after 36 holes, 4 shots behind the T4 line at -11 and 8 behind the leader, with roughly 20-30 players ahead of him. On a course where the top-5 line usually lands at 20-23 under, he likely needs a weekend around 64-65 while several of the -10 to -12 group stall. His recent form (about -0.2 SG per round, no top-5s in 2026) and his weak El Cardonal history (T42, T56) put him below an average player in this spot. The low-scoring, high-variance course, ties at fifth, and his strong motivation to save his card offset this slightly. Round 3 results, which I don't have, are the main unknown and could move this sharply either way.

Only 22 days remain, and nothing that would count as a solution is scheduled. CMI recognition is impossible this month under its two-year rule. The main path to YES is a new AI-lab claim, most plausibly OpenAI's long-teased second problem (likely Hodge), perhaps timed to a next-GPT launch. That announcement has slipped for about 7-8 weeks amid backlash, retractions and erosion of the Navier-Stokes claim, so the odds of it landing in November and of a resolver accepting it as 'solved' are both reduced. Navier-Stokes was claimed in September, and a November verification or CMI update being counted as a November solution is a small residual path.

Breakdowns in this conflict have come from deliberate, politically timed large operations rather than gradual erosion, so the main risk is a post-midterm joint US-Israeli strike round, which multiple outlets reported being planned for early November (possibly around Nov 9). I put about a 20% chance on such a round starting within the window. Israeli participation and/or Iranian missiles hitting Israel would very likely follow, making NO near-certain on that path. Against this, Rubio says no decision has been made, key cabinet members favour continuing the blockade, Qatar is mediating an active draft deal, and recent US strikes have been 'minor', US-only, and answered by Iran in the Gulf rather than at Israel. With only about 7.5 days left and other paths (Lebanon spiral, unilateral Israeli action) adding a few percent, I estimate about an 80% chance the ceasefire holds.

Harvard (7-1, FCS-ranked, Ivy title race) is clearly better than Penn (4-4, -16 point differential), outperforming it by ~10-15 points against common opponents. Penn's weak rushing attack (38 and 58 yards in its last two games) and Harvard's strong defense and title motivation favor Harvard. Penn gets home field and Homecoming, plays many close games, and nearly beat Harvard in 2024 and 2025 (lost by 3 and 2). Harvard's turnover-prone sophomore QB adds some upset variance. The most likely upset path is a Harvard turnover-fueled one-score loss, which is plausible but not likely, so I sit slightly above the bare spread-implied rate.

A tie requires the two blocs to land on exactly the same seat count, which is improbable even in a close race. Current private polls centre on a Right lead of about 40-60 seats (PP+Vox around 195-205), and even the most left-friendly private pollster (SW Demoscopia) implies about Right +20. A repeat of the 2023 polling error (15-25 seats toward the left) still leaves the Right well ahead. Only the pro-PSOE-biased CIS shows a left lead, and that scenario overshoots a tie. Fat tails, three weeks of campaign and the parity requirement on uncounted seats leave a probability well under 1%.

The question is truncated, but the 'NNN' prefix and Nov 30 close strongly suggest a personal No Nut November market about someone named Eyal, resolved on self-report. Failing is the cultural norm for NNN, and there's a meaningful chance (~15-20%) he has already failed without the market being resolved. Conditional on surviving the first week, the odds of finishing improve to roughly a coin flip, helped by social pressure, possible self-betting, lenient self-reporting, and the market closing before the final evening. A small weight on the Eyal Zamir reading (where YES is ~95%) nudges the estimate up slightly. Overall I land just below 50%.

Gemini 4 Argon, Google's new flagship, went public on Oct 13 but is not branded 'Pro'. The market remaining open almost four weeks later (Kalshi-style wording, which usually settles promptly) suggests the resolver requires a 'Pro'-named model, so the Argon path gets only ~6%. A Pro-named release by Nov 30 looks unlikely: 3.5 Pro was reportedly cancelled and superseded, no 'Gemini 4 Pro' rename or sibling has leaked, no LMArena or AI Studio signals or event invites have appeared, and Thanksgiving week shrinks the window. Google's historical late-year launches cluster in early-to-mid December, after close. Combining the Argon-interpretation tail with a ~7-8% chance of a genuine Pro-named launch gives ~13%.

The job has been empty since Oct 16, and the window closes at day 45 of the vacancy, about where the last vacancy ended (~43 days). Trump is actively trying to fill it: he publicly offered the job to Dana White, and they meet Nov 9. But White running UFC/TKO and CNN's report that he declined make a formal acceptance less likely than not (~25%). If White passes, Trump may pivot quickly to avoid further embarrassment, and Stephen Miller's arrival as chief of staff could speed staffing. Still, the second term has shown slow searches, comfort with no briefer, and the risk of an 'acting' pick that doesn't count. Thanksgiving and post-midterm turmoil shorten the effective window.

No NO trigger (FDA, overseen trial, human efficacy data) is plausible in 20 days, so the question is whether the creator calls YES at close. Arguable YES evidence exists: the website went offline in May 2026, sales are paused after a colonization failure, and critical dossiers exist. But the creator has not resolved on any of it for months, which suggests a conservative reading or inactivity. The company publicly says it still exists and is building a v2, which undercuts both 'scam' and 'disappeared.' A new major-outlet exposé or a formal shutdown within three weeks is unlikely. Remaining mass goes to NO-by-default, N/A, or a close extension.

Zhu is the higher-ranked (≈467 vs ≈691) [3] qualifying seed with a solid 2026 record, which on ranking alone gives him about 60%. But Fancutt's ranking is deflated by a spring 2026 collapse to 1,728 he has been recovering from (M25 title, 15-8 record), so the true skill gap is narrower than the numbers imply. Fancutt also has home conditions in Brisbane, a serve-oriented game suited to fast hard courts, and won their only meeting. Zhu arrives on a run of 4-5 straight Challenger qualifying losses after travelling from Asia. Netting these out gives roughly a coin flip; the match may already have been played, and the actual result should override this.

In the most recent election in the same territory (Andalusian regional, May 2026), Almería went PP 42.7%, Vox 23.2%, PSOE 21.7%, so PSOE was third and about 21 points behind PP. Current provincial projections (Sigma Dos: PP 3, Vox 2, PSOE 1; SocioMétrica: Vox 28%, PSOE 22%, PP first) agree, and PSOE's national numbers worsened after the Urda crash. YES requires either PSOE overtaking PP or a 2-2-2 split with PSOE first on votes, which means a swing of 12 points or more against PP in three weeks. Small-sample provincial poll error and source uncertainty in the brief are real but cannot close a gap this size. A small residual allows for a major scandal, a polling collapse or data errors.
